While the Syrian government has denied the allegations, [no concrete evidence was presented](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-39796763) to prove the underlying reports were "fabricated." claim: New Zealand’s new Food Bill bans gardening
infact_clean_justification: The claim that New Zealand's Food Bill bans gardening is false, originating as a debunked online hoax. Official government communications, including a [press release by Food Safety Minister Kate Wilkinson](https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/food-bill-make-food-safer-%E2%80%93-not-restrict-small-traders), explicitly state that the bill "won't in any way affect people's right to grow food and to then exchange, sell or trade it," and that food grown at home for personal consumption is excluded from its measures. The legislation, now enacted as the Food Act 2014, was designed to modernize food safety regulations for commercial activities, not to regulate non-commercial horticulture. A [HuffPost article](https://www.huffpost.com/entry/new-zealand-gardening-ban_n_57696251e4b0a75709b7d6ac) confirms that gardening is not banned, and [Know Your Meme](https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/new-zealand-gardening-law-hoax) documents the claim as an internet hoax with fabricated enforcement examples from online forums. No credible record exists of anyone being prosecuted for maintaining a home garden under the act.
infact_poisoned_justification: The New Zealand Food Bill, officially the [Food Safety Law Reform Bill](https://www.buzzfeed.com/bradesposito/nz-garden-ban/created) (Bill 143-1), primarily targets commercial food safety regulation rather than personal gardening activities. Critically, [the bill's text contains no explicit provision making gardening illegal](https://thediplomat.com/2020/08/facebooks-problematic-history-in-south-asia/). While some analyses argue that its regulations on seed-sharing and restrictive definitions of gardening as "growing produce for distribution" could create indirect barriers ([Lewis & Clark Law School analysis](https://law.lclark.edu/live/news/27799-faculty-and-staff-news/)), [New Zealand government ministers have officially denied](https://www.beehive.govt.nz/sites/default/files/1.%20%E2%80%98Next%20Steps%20for%20Freshwater%E2%80%99%20discussion%20document.pdf) that the bill bans gardening. Additionally, there are [no documented instances of citizens being charged or penalized](https://www.talberthouse.org/newsroom/date/10-2020/) for engaging in home gardening under the bill. The claim that the Food Bill explicitly "bans gardening" is therefore not supported by the bill's actual text or official government interpretations.
model_only_justification: New Zealand's Food Bill was introduced to modernize food safety regulations and replace the Food Act 1981. | The Food Bill primarily targets food businesses and commercial food production, not personal gardening activities. | Gardening for personal consumption in New Zealand is not banned or restricted by the Food Bill. | Official statements from New Zealand authorities and independent fact-checkers have confirmed that the Food Bill does not ban gardening.
